chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Baseer, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'I dislike that I rent a single millstone, then I hire it out for more than what I had hired it for, unless something new is introduced in it, or a loss is incurred in it.'

key_terms.تُغْرَمَ فِيهَا غَرَامَةٌ: A loss/penalty is incurred in it (additional costs)
key_terms.يُحْدَثَ فِيهَا حَدَثٌ: Something new is introduced in it (improvements/changes)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on sub-leasing rented property for profit?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the permissibility of sub-leasing (*ta’jir*) by expressing a preference against profiting solely from the lease contract unless justified by tangible enhancements or incurred liabilities. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic principle that profit in leasing should be linked to actual value addition or risk, distinguishing it from mere arbitrage. The exception for 'events' (*hadath*) or 'compensation' (*gharamah*) provides flexibility for practical scenarios where the lessee assumes additional burdens or improves the asset.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at, from Abu Baseer who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> dislike that I<sup>asws</sup> rent one grinding stone, then I<sup>asws</sup> hire it out for more than what I had hired it for unless I<sup>asws</sup> introduce something new in it, or make a loss in it’.
en.sarwar: 9. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Sama‘ah from abu Basir who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘I dislike renting a grinding stone, then renting it out to someone else for more than what I has rented for, unless some improvement is made or loss has taken place.’”
